source.title: Detecting Spacecraft Anomalies Using LSTMs and Nonparametric Dynamic Thresholding
source.venue: Proceedings of the 24th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining (KDD '18)

confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed, heavily-cited (900+) operational deployment of exactly the architecture MECH-042 proposes: a fleet of low-bandwidth read-only telemetry channels on a safety-critical autonomous system, monitored by automated detectors, with the explicit operational purpose of reducing risk and monitoring burden. Its evidential value for MECH-042 is that this is a WORKING, deployed instance of the pattern in an engineering system rather than a biological one, evaluated against expert-labelled ground truth from two real missions (SMAP, MSL Curiosity), and that the authors treat false-positive mitigation as a first-class design problem rather than an afterthought -- the same posture MECH-042's matched-false-alarm-rate requirement takes. Confidence held to 0.68 because the paper evaluates DETECTION quality (precision/recall against labelled anomalies) and not LEAD TIME against a behaviour-stream detector, which is the specific quantity MECH-042 sub-claim (2) needs; it therefore corroborates the pattern's viability without testing the claim's comparative proposition.
failure_signatures: The paper's central operational problem is false positives, not missed detections: the authors devote explicit machinery to false-positive mitigation because an anomaly detector on a large telemetry fleet that alarms too often is operationally useless regardless of its sensitivity. MECH-042's telemetry detector faces the same asymmetry across its seven-plus named channels (current_precision, running_variance, is_committed / beta_elevated, e3_steps_per_tick, CommitReadiness.get_state, SalienceCoordinator operating_mode, residue coverage), and a per-channel detector bank will alarm far more often than a single behaviour-stream detector unless the multiple-comparison cost is paid in the threshold.

Thresholds had to be set nonparametrically and dynamically because static thresholds on telemetry channels do not hold across operating regimes. REE's channels have the same property -- what counts as anomalous current_precision early in a life is not what counts as anomalous late in it -- so a fixed pre-registered threshold risks either missing the pathology or firing throughout the developmental ramp.

Ground truth was expert-labelled anomalies from real missions, and the authors are explicit that this labelling is incomplete. MECH-042 avoids this failure mode entirely by injecting its pathology at a known tick, which is a genuine methodological advantage worth stating rather than assuming.

The system detects anomalies in telemetry; it does not establish that telemetry beats the behaviour stream, because for a spacecraft there is effectively no separate behaviour stream to compare against. The pattern's operational success is therefore weaker evidence for MECH-042's COMPARATIVE claim than it first appears.

mapping.source_claim_statement: LSTM-based prediction models applied to expert-labelled spacecraft telemetry channels from the SMAP satellite and the MSL Curiosity rover, combined with an unsupervised nonparametric dynamic thresholding scheme and explicit false-positive mitigation, detect operational anomalies well enough to reduce the monitoring burden on operations engineers and lower operational risk.
mapping.ree_translation: This is MECH-042's mechanism, deployed and working, in an engineering system. A safety-critical autonomous system exposes a large number of low-bandwidth read-only internal-state channels; those channels feed automated detectors; the detectors exist purely to catch internal faults early, and add no actuation pathway of their own. The paper corroborates the architectural premise -- that a telemetry surface is a legitimate safety instrument for an autonomous system whose internal faults would otherwise only be discovered through their consequences -- and, more usefully, supplies two operational lessons MECH-042's experiment design should absorb: that false positives dominate the engineering problem once the channel count is large, and that static thresholds on regime-dependent channels do not work.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The load-bearing gap: this paper does NOT measure lead time of a telemetry detector against a matched detector on a behaviour stream, because a spacecraft has no behaviour stream in the relevant sense -- telemetry is essentially the only observable. MECH-042 sub-claim (2) is specifically a COMPARATIVE claim (positive lead time over a behaviour-stream detector at matched false-alarm rate), and this paper cannot speak to the comparison, only to the viability of one of its two arms. It should be cited as evidence that the telemetry-detector arm is buildable and operationally worthwhile, never as evidence that it wins. Secondary caveats: an LSTM predictive-residual detector is far heavier than the pre-registered detector MECH-042 envisages and its performance figures do not transfer; the anomalies are real-mission and exogenous rather than injected; and 'anomaly' in this setting means departure from learned nominal behaviour, which is a weaker target than identifying a specific injected control-plane pathology.
mapping.source_context: Operational anomaly detection on real telemetry from two NASA missions -- the Soil Moisture Active Passive satellite and the Mars Science Laboratory rover Curiosity -- with expert-labelled anomaly ground truth; engineering deployment, not a controlled experiment.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.8: peer-reviewed at a top data-mining venue, very highly cited, and validated against real operational data rather than a benchmark -- but it is an engineering-deployment paper, so it reports what worked in production rather than a controlled comparison. Mapping fidelity is the binding constraint at 0.55: the architectural pattern maps almost exactly, but the comparative proposition at the heart of sub-claim (2) is simply not tested here. Transfer risk 0.35: engineering telemetry to an artificial cognitive control plane is a modest jump, and the operational lessons (false-positive dominance, regime-dependent thresholds) transfer more readily than the method does.
